mainTopic: Marrying off a son, the duty to teach children and grandchildren תורה, and how to learn and know תורה
overview: The amud opens with the end of רב חסדא's remark about marrying young. רבא then advises marrying off a son while the father still has influence over him, ages 16–22 or 18–24, which matches a dispute between תנאים about 'חנוך לנער'. Next the גמרא asks how much תורה a father must teach his son. שמואל points to זבולון בן דן, and after a challenge the גמרא concludes the required amount is only מקרא, though even a grandfather must teach. A ברייתא that seems to exempt grandfathers is answered by another ברייתא, which learns grandsons from 'ולבני בניך' and leaves out daughters. רבי יהושע בן לוי teaches that teaching a grandson is like receiving the תורה at הר סיני, and stories show חכמים putting this first each day. The גמרא then reads ושננתם as ושלשתם: every day should be split among מקרא, משנה and תלמוד. This leads to the סופרים who counted the letters, words and verses of the תורה, and רב יוסף shows we can no longer settle where the exact middle falls. The amud ends with a ברייתא saying תורה must be sharp in your mouth, and its proof-verse comes on the next amud.

steps.title: The end of רב חסדא's remark: an arrow in the שטן's eye
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא finishes his statement: had he married even younger, he could have defied the שטן completely.
steps.simpleTranslation: I would have said to the שטן: An arrow in your eye!
steps.whatsHappening: This line finishes רב חסדא's statement from just before. He said he was better than his friends because he married at sixteen, and if he had married at fourteen he would have mocked the שטן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'An arrow in your eye' is a way of saying 'I am not afraid of you at all.' Marrying very young would have protected him almost completely from the יצר הרע. This sets up the theme of the next lines: marry off your son early.

keyTerms.meaning: The Satan, here standing for the יצר הרע (evil inclination)

phrases.english: I would have said to the Satan:
phrases.notes: These are still רב חסדא's words: if he had married at fourteen, he would have said this.

phrases.english: An arrow in your eye!
phrases.notes: A way of saying 'I'm not scared of you at all.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes רב חסדא's statement about marrying young, begun before this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Marrying very young gives a person strong protection against the יצר הרע.

steps.title: רבא's advice: marry off your son while you still have control
steps.stepSummary: רבא tells רבי נתן בר אמי to marry off his son while the father still has influence over him.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said to רבי נתן בר אמי: While your hand is still on your son's neck (find him a wife).
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives practical advice: arrange your son's marriage while he still listens to you.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Your hand on your son's neck' is a picture of a father who still has authority over his son. Once the son is older and independent, the father can no longer guide him. The next step will explain what age this is.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רָבָא לְרַבִּי נָתָן בַּר אַמֵּי:
phrases.english: Rava said to Rabbi Natan bar Ami:
While your hand is still on your son's neck.
phrases.notes: He means: while you still have control over your son, find him a wife.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רָבָא לְרַבִּי נָתָן בַּר אַמֵּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the theme of marrying young with practical advice to a father.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A father should marry off his son while he still has authority over him.

steps.title: What age is that? Two versions
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא defines the 'hand on the neck' years: from 16 to 22, or, by another version, from 18 to 24.
steps.simpleTranslation: From sixteen until twenty-two; and some say: from eighteen until twenty-four.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains which years count as the time a father still has influence over his son, and gives two versions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first version says ages 16–22; a second tradition ('ואמרי לה') says 18–24. Both agree there is a limited window, and they only differ by two years. The next step will show this matches a dispute between תנאים.

keyTerms.meaning: And some say (another version of the tradition)

phrases.english: From sixteen until twenty-two,

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמְרִי לַהּ: מִתַּמְנֵי סְרֵי עַד עֶשְׂרִים וְאַרְבָּעָה.
phrases.english: and some say: from eighteen until twenty-four.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defines the time period in רבא's advice.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The window of a father's influence is 16–22, or by another version 18–24.

steps.title: This matches a dispute between תנאים about 'חנוך לנער'
steps.stepSummary: The same two age ranges appear in a dispute between רבי יהודה and רבי נחמיה about the פסוק 'Train a child in his way'.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is like a dispute between תנאים: 'Train a child in the way he should go.' רבי יהודה and רבי נחמיה: one said from sixteen until twenty-two, and one said from eighteen until twenty-four.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that the two versions about the right age already appear as a dispute between תנאים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה and רבי נחמיה argue about what age the פסוק in משלי means when it says to train a child. Their two opinions are exactly the two age ranges from the previous step. So the time when a father can educate his son is also the time to marry him off.

keyTerms.meaning: It is like (a dispute between) תנאים

phrases.english: This is like a dispute between Tannaim:
"Train a child in the way he should go,"
phrases.notes: משלי 22:6

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda and Rabbi Nechemya disagree:

phrases.aramaic: חַד אָמַר: מִשִּׁיתְּסַר וְעַד עֶשְׂרִים וְתַרְתֵּין,
phrases.english: one said: from sixteen until twenty-two,

phrases.aramaic: וְחַד אָמַר: מִתַּמְנֵי סְרֵי וְעַד עֶשְׂרִים וְאַרְבְּעָה.
phrases.english: and one said: from eighteen until twenty-four.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows the two age versions match an earlier dispute between תנאים.
steps.raayaObject: The two age ranges for a father's influence over his son.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The dispute between רבי יהודה and רבי נחמיה on 'חנוך לנער על פי דרכו'.
steps.whatToRemember: The years a father can still guide his son (16–22 or 18–24) are the years to train him and to marry him off.

steps.title: How much תורה must a father teach his son?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how far a father's duty to teach his son תורה goes.
steps.simpleTranslation: Up to what point is a person obligated to teach his son תורה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new question: what is the limit of a father's duty to teach his son תורה?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier the גמרא learned that a father must teach his son תורה. Now it wants to know the extent: just the written תורה, or more? The answer comes in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: Up to what point / how far

phrases.english: Up to what point is a person obligated
to teach his son Torah?

steps.triggerLanguage: עַד הֵיכָן חַיָּיב אָדָם לְלַמֵּד אֶת בְּנוֹ תּוֹרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the topic of age to the scope of a father's teaching duty.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The extent of a father's duty to teach his son תורה.

steps.title: שמואל: like זבולון בן דן, whose grandfather taught him everything
steps.stepSummary: שמואל says the model is זבולון בן דן, whose grandfather taught him מקרא, משנה, תלמוד, הלכות and אגדות.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: For example, זבולון בן דן, whose father's father taught him מקרא, משנה, תלמוד, הלכות and אגדות.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל answers by pointing to a real person, זבולון בן דן, as an example of how a son should be taught.
steps.deeperAnalysis: זבולון בן דן was taught by his grandfather, and he was taught every area of תורה. On the surface, שמואל seems to say a father must teach his son all of these. The next step will challenge that.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said:
For example, Zevulun ben Dan,
phrases.notes: A man from שמואל's own time, not the tribes זבולון and דן.

phrases.english: whose father's father taught him
Bible, Mishna, Talmud, halachot and aggadot.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל כְּגוֹן זְבוּלוּן בֶּן דָּן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of how much a father must teach.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The model is זבולון בן דן, whose grandfather taught him all areas of תורה.
steps.confusionAlert: זבולון בן דן here is one person living in שמואל's time, not the two שבטים.

steps.title: A ברייתא says מקרא alone is enough
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says once a father taught his son מקרא he need not teach him משנה, and רבא explains מקרא means just the תורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: They raised an objection: If he taught him מקרא, he does not have to teach him משנה. And רבא said: מקרא means the תורה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges שמואל with a ברייתא showing that a father's duty is much smaller than what זבולון בן דן was taught.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says teaching מקרא is enough and משנה is not required. רבא adds that מקרא here means only the תורה (חומש). So the basic duty is only the תורה, which seems to clash with שמואל's example of teaching everything.

keyTerms.meaning: They raised an objection (from a ברייתא)
He does not (need to) teach him

phrases.english: They raised an objection: If he taught him Bible,
he does not have to teach him Mishna.
And Rava said: "Bible" means the Torah!
phrases.notes: רבא means just the five books of the תורה, not נביאים or כתובים.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges שמואל's answer.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's statement that the model is זבולון בן דן, who was taught everything.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא, as explained by רבא, limits the father's duty to the תורה alone, so it cannot require משנה, תלמוד, הלכות and אגדות.

steps.title: Like זבולון בן דן in one way, not in another
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains שמואל: the son should be taught like זבולון בן דן in that even a grandfather teaches, but not in the amount, which is only מקרא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Like זבולון בן דן, and not like זבולון בן דן. Like זבולון בן דן, in that his father's father taught him; and not like זבולון בן דן, because there he learned מקרא, משנה, תלמוד, הלכות and אגדות, while here it is מקרא alone.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by saying שמואל's example is only partly a model.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל brought זבולון בן דן to show who is obligated: even a grandfather must teach his grandson. He did not mean that everything זבולון learned is required; the required amount is only מקרא, as the ברייתא says. So שמואל and the ברייתא no longer clash.

keyTerms.meaning: And not like זבולון בן דן

phrases.aramaic: כִּזְבוּלוּן בֶּן דָּן, וְלֹא כִּזְבוּלוּן בֶּן דָּן.
phrases.english: Like Zevulun ben Dan, and not like Zevulun ben Dan.

phrases.aramaic: כִּזְבוּלוּן בֶּן דָּן – שֶׁלִּמְּדוֹ אֲבִי אָבִיו,
phrases.english: Like Zevulun ben Dan, in that his father's father taught him,
and not like Zevulun ben Dan,
for whereas there
he learned Bible, Mishna, Talmud, halachot and aggadot,
while here, the duty is Bible alone.
phrases.notes: 'Here' means the duty described in the ברייתא.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּזְבוּלוּן בֶּן דָּן, וְלֹא כִּזְבוּלוּן בֶּן דָּן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from the ברייתא by narrowing what שמואל meant.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the example: it is a model for one point only.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: שמואל seemed to say a father must teach everything זבולון בן דן learned.
steps.terutzMaskana: שמואל's example teaches only that a grandfather is also obligated; the required content is מקרא alone.
steps.whatToRemember: A grandfather also has a duty to teach his grandson, but the basic required amount is only מקרא (the תורה).
steps.whyThisMatters: It sets the two limits of the duty to teach: who must teach (father and grandfather) and how much is required (the תורה itself).

steps.title: Is a grandfather really obligated to teach?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the idea that a grandfather must teach his grandson. A ברייתא says the obligation is only toward one's sons, and the פסוק about grandsons only describes a reward.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is a grandfather really obligated? A ברייתא teaches: 'And you shall teach them to your sons' means your sons and not your grandsons. Then what does 'make them known to your sons and your sons' sons' mean? It teaches that whoever teaches his son תורה gets credit as if he taught his son, his grandson, and all future generations.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the conclusion of step 8, that a grandfather must teach like זבולון בן דן's grandfather did. It brings a ברייתא that seems to say grandfathers have no such duty.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 8 kept only one part of שמואל's model: even a grandfather teaches. This ברייתא reads 'your sons' as a limit that leaves out grandsons. It explains the grandson פסוק as a reward for teaching your son, not as a new obligation.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And you shall teach them to your sons' (דברים 11:19)
'Make them known to your sons and your sons' sons' (דברים 4:9)
the פסוק counts it for him as if
so how do I explain (the other פסוק)?

phrases.english: But is his father's father obligated?
But isn't it taught in a ברייתא:
"And you shall teach them to your sons"
phrases.notes: דברים 11:19

phrases.english: but not your sons' sons.
And how do I explain:
"Make them known to your sons and to your sons' sons"?
phrases.notes: דברים 4:9

phrases.english: It comes to tell you:
that whoever teaches his son תורה,
the פסוק counts it for him

phrases.aramaic: כְּאִילּוּ לִמְּדוֹ לוֹ וְלִבְנוֹ וּלְבֶן בְּנוֹ,
phrases.english: as if he taught him, and his son, and his son's son,
until the end of all generations!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the part of שמואל's view that step 8 kept, that a grandfather also teaches.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim from step 8 that a grandfather is obligated to teach his grandson.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא limits the obligation to 'your sons' and reads the grandson פסוק as a reward, not a duty.

steps.title: שמואל follows a different ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that שמואל holds like another תנא, who learns the duty to teach grandsons from the second פסוק and reads 'your sons' as excluding daughters.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל holds like this תנא, as a ברייתא teaches: 'And you shall teach them to your sons'. That only tells me sons. How do I know grandsons? The פסוק says 'to your sons and to your sons' sons.' If so, why does it say 'your sons'? To teach: your sons, and not your daughters.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by showing that תנאים argue about this. שמואל simply follows the ברייתא that obligates grandfathers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both ברייתות use the same two פסוקים but read them differently. The first reads 'your sons' as excluding grandsons. The second learns grandsons from 'your sons' sons' and uses 'your sons' to exclude daughters. So שמואל's view has a solid source.

keyTerms.meaning: like this תנא (agreeing with a particular Tannaic opinion)

steps.confusionAlert: Both ברייתות quote the exact same פסוקים. The disagreement is only about what the word 'your sons' comes to exclude: grandsons or daughters.
steps.whyThisMatters: This ברייתא is a main source that a father is not obligated to teach his daughters תורה the way he must teach his sons.

phrases.english: He holds like this תנא,
phrases.notes: 'He' is שמואל, whose זבולון בן דן model has a grandfather doing the teaching.

phrases.english: as it is taught in a ברייתא:
"And you shall teach them to your sons":
from this I would only know your sons;
from where do we know your sons' sons?
The פסוק teaches:
"Make them known to your sons and to your sons' sons."
If so, why does the פסוק say "your sons"?
To teach: your sons, and not your daughters.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 9 by finding a different ברייתא that supports שמואל.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Dispute of תנאים: the challenge comes from one ברייתא, while שמואל follows another.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Grandfathers have no duty to teach, because the ברייתא limits it to sons.
steps.terutzMaskana: Another תנא obligates grandfathers from 'your sons' sons', and שמואל follows him.
steps.whatToRemember: שמואל's view that a grandfather must teach rests on a ברייתא that learns grandsons from 'וְלִבְנֵי בָנֶיךָ' and reads 'בְּנֵיכֶם' as excluding daughters.

steps.title: Teaching a grandson is like receiving the Torah at Sinai
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע בן לוי teaches that whoever teaches his grandson תורה is counted as if he received it at הר סיני. He learns this from the פסוק about grandsons, which sits right next to the פסוק about standing at חורב.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע בן לוי said: Anyone who teaches his son's son תורה, the פסוק counts it for him as if he received it at הר סיני. It says 'make them known to your sons and your sons' sons,' and right next to it: 'the day you stood before ה׳ your God at חורב.'
steps.whatsHappening: Now that teaching a grandson is shown to be a real duty, רבי יהושע בן לוי adds how great its reward is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He builds on the closeness of two פסוקים. The פסוק about teaching grandsons is placed right next to the one about standing at חורב, which is הר סיני. So passing תורה to a grandson is linked to receiving it at Sinai.

keyTerms.meaning: and right next to it (in the פסוקים)

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said:

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל הַמְלַמֵּד אֶת בֶּן בְּנוֹ תּוֹרָה
phrases.english: Anyone who teaches his son's son תורה,
the פסוק counts it for him
as if he received it at Mount Sinai,
as it says:
"Make them known to your sons and to your sons' sons,"
and right next to it:

phrases.aramaic: ״יוֹם אֲשֶׁר עָמַדְתָּ לִפְנֵי ה׳ אֱלֹקֶיךָ בְּחֹרֵב״.
phrases.english: "The day that you stood before ה׳ your God at Horeb."
phrases.notes: דברים 4:10. חורב is another name for הר סיני.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי: כׇּל הַמְלַמֵּד אֶת בֶּן בְּנוֹ תּוֹרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After grandfathers are shown to be obligated, this step adds the reward for teaching a grandson.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Teaching one's grandson תורה is counted as if one received it at הר סיני, based on the closeness of דברים 4:9 and 4:10.

steps.title: רבי יהושע בן לוי rushes his grandchild to learn
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא בר אבא sees רבי יהושע בן לוי hurrying a child to the synagogue with just a simple cloth on his head. When asked why he rushes, he points to the same two neighboring פסוקים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חייא בר אבא found רבי יהושע בן לוי with a simple cloth thrown on his head, bringing the child to the synagogue. He asked: Why all this? He answered: Is it a small thing what is written, 'make them known to your sons,' and right next to it, 'the day you stood before ה׳ your God at חורב'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story showing that רבי יהושע בן לוי lived by his own teaching.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He did not even stop to dress properly, because he saw bringing the child to learn as standing at Sinai. His answer repeats the same two פסוקים from step 11, so the story backs up his teaching with action.

keyTerms.meaning: he found him, came across him
a simple cloth or head covering

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא אַשְׁכְּחֵיהּ לְרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי
phrases.english: Rabbi Chiya bar Abba found Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi
who had thrown a simple cloth on his head

phrases.aramaic: וְקָא מַמְטֵי לֵיהּ לְיָנוֹקָא לְבֵי כְנִישְׁתָּא.
phrases.english: and was bringing the child to the synagogue.
phrases.notes: This fits his own teaching. The child seems to be his grandson.

phrases.english: He said to him: Why all this rush?
He said to him:
Is it a small thing, what is written:
"Make them known to your sons,"
and right next to it:

phrases.aramaic: ״יוֹם אֲשֶׁר עָמַדְתָּ לִפְנֵי ה׳ אֱלֹקֶיךָ בְּחֹרֵב״?
phrases.english: "The day that you stood before ה׳ your God at Horeb"?

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא אַשְׁכְּחֵיהּ לְרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows רבי יהושע בן לוי acting on the teaching he gave in step 11.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יהושע בן לוי's teaching that teaching a grandson is like standing at Sinai.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A story of his own urgent behavior, explained with the same two neighboring פסוקים.

steps.title: No breakfast before teaching the child
steps.stepSummary: After this encounter, רבי חייא בר אבא would not eat breakfast until he had reviewed with the child and added new learning. רבה בר רב הונא would not eat until he had brought the child to the בית מדרש.
steps.simpleTranslation: From then on, רבי חייא בר אבא would not taste meat until he had read with the child and added to his learning. רבה בר רב הונא would not taste meat until he had brought the child to the בית מדרש.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא closes the topic by showing how other חכמים put this teaching into daily practice.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The story changed רבי חייא בר אבא's habits. Teaching the child came before his own morning meal. רבה בר רב הונא had the same priority, so teaching children came before personal needs.

keyTerms.meaning: meat; here it means the morning meal
reads with, reviews the פסוקים with

steps.whatToRemember: Teaching children and grandchildren תורה is so great that it is compared to standing at הר סיני. חכמים made it their first task of the day, even before eating.

phrases.english: From then on,

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא לָא טָעֵים אוּמְצָא
phrases.english: Rabbi Chiya bar Abba would not taste meat
phrases.notes: In other words, he would not eat his morning meal.

phrases.english: until he had read with the child and added to his learning.

phrases.aramaic: רַבָּה בַּר רַב הוּנָא לָא טָעֵים אוּמְצָא
phrases.english: Rabba bar Rav Huna would not taste meat
until he had brought the child to the study hall.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִכָּאן וְאֵילָךְ, רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא לָא טָעֵים אוּמְצָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tells the lasting effect of the story in step 12 on רבי חייא בר אבא, and adds the similar practice of רבה בר רב הונא.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: חכמים put teaching children ahead of their own breakfast, showing how highly they valued רבי יהושע בן לוי's lesson.

steps.title: Learning should be split into three
steps.stepSummary: רב ספרא, quoting רבי יהושע בן חנניה, reads ושננתם ('teach them diligently') as ושלשתם ('divide them into three').
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ספרא said in the name of רבי יהושע בן חנניה: What does the פסוק mean when it says 'And you shall teach them diligently to your sons'? Don't read it as 'veshinantam'. Read it as 'veshillashtam', meaning divide it into three.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new teaching that reads a word in the פסוק of שמע in a fresh way, so that it tells us to split Torah learning into three parts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word ושננתם sounds close to ושלשתם, which comes from שלוש (three). Using an אל תקרי reading, רבי יהושע בן חנניה draws a second message from the פסוק without cancelling its plain meaning. It is the source for the next step's rule about thirds.

keyTerms.meaning: And you shall teach them diligently (sharpen them)
Do not read it as... (a way of drawing an extra lesson from a word)
And you shall divide them into three

steps.confusionAlert: אל תקרי does not mean the פסוק is spelled wrong or that the plain meaning is gone. It adds a second lesson on top of the plain meaning.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב סָפְרָא מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן חֲנַנְיָא:
phrases.english: Rav Safra said in the name of Rabbi Yehoshua ben Chananya:
What is the meaning of what is written: "And you shall teach them diligently to your sons"?
phrases.notes: דברים 6:7

phrases.english: Do not read it as "veshinantam" (teach diligently),
but rather as "veshillashtam" (divide into three).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the theme of teaching one's children and grandchildren to how a person should organize his own learning, using the same פסוק of ושננתם לבניך.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The word ושננתם is also read as ושלשתם: Torah learning should be divided into three parts.

steps.title: A third for Bible, a third for משנה, a third for Talmud
steps.stepSummary: From the reading ושלשתם comes the rule that a person should divide his years among מקרא, משנה and תלמוד.
steps.simpleTranslation: A person should always divide his years into three: a third for Bible, a third for משנה, and a third for Talmud.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא spells out what 'dividing into three' means in practice: time should be split evenly among three kinds of Torah learning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מקרא is the written תנ״ך, משנה is the short rulings of the Oral Torah, and תלמוד is understanding the reasons behind them. The rule says all three deserve equal time, and that one should not focus on only one.

keyTerms.meaning: The basic teachings of the Oral Torah
The study of the reasons and analysis behind the משנה

phrases.english: A person should always divide his years into three:
a third for Bible, a third for Mishnah,
a third for Talmud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns the reading ושלשתם from step 14 into a practical rule.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A person should divide his learning time equally among מקרא, משנה and תלמוד.

steps.title: Nobody knows how long he will live
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how a person can divide his years into thirds if he does not know how many years he has.
steps.simpleTranslation: Who knows how long he will live?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the rule from the last step: dividing your 'years' into thirds seems impossible.
steps.deeperAnalysis: To know what a third of your life is, you would need to know the length of your whole life. No one knows that, so the rule as worded cannot be carried out.

phrases.english: Who knows how long he will live?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the wording 'his years' in step 15.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that a person should divide his years into three.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: You cannot calculate a third of your life without knowing its total length, and no one knows that.

steps.title: The division is done each day
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the rule is about days: each day should be split into thirds.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, the rule is needed for days.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question by explaining that the three-way split applies to each day, not to one's whole lifetime.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since a person can easily divide a single day, the problem goes away. The word 'years' is understood to mean the days that make up one's years.

keyTerms.meaning: It is only needed for... (narrowing what a rule is about)

steps.whatToRemember: The rule of ושלשתם means every day should include מקרא, משנה and תלמוד.

phrases.english: No, it is needed for days.
phrases.notes: He means each single day should be split into three parts of learning.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 16.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting the scope of the rule (years → days)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The rule seemed to require dividing one's whole lifespan into thirds.
steps.terutzMaskana: The division is applied to each day, which anyone can do.

steps.title: Why the early sages were called סופרים
steps.stepSummary: Because the early sages spent so much time on מקרא, they were called סופרים, 'counters', since they counted the letters, words and verses of the תורה and of תהלים.
steps.simpleTranslation: That is why the early sages were called 'soferim': they counted all the letters in the Torah. They would say: the vav of 'gachon' is the middle letter of a Torah scroll. 'Darosh darash' is the middle of the words. 'Vehisgalach' is the middle of the verses. In 'The boar from the forest gnaws at it', the ayin of 'ya'ar' is the middle of תהלים. 'But He, merciful, forgives sin' is the middle verse.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא links the time spent on מקרא to the name סופרים, and gives examples of how carefully the early sages counted the text.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word סופרים can mean 'counters', from לספור. The examples show how exact their knowledge was: they knew the middle letter, middle word and middle verse of the תורה, and the middle letter and middle verse of תהלים.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows how seriously the earliest sages took the exact wording of the text. This sets up רב יוסף's question in the next step.

phrases.english: Therefore the early ones were called "soferim,"
phrases.notes: Here סופרים means 'counters', from לספור, to count.

phrases.english: because they would count all the letters in the Torah,
as they would say:
the vav of "gachon" (belly)
phrases.notes: ויקרא 11:42

phrases.aramaic: חֶצְיָין שֶׁל אוֹתִיּוֹת שֶׁל סֵפֶר תּוֹרָה.
phrases.english: is the midpoint of the letters of a Torah scroll.
"Darosh darash" (diligently inquired)
phrases.notes: ויקרא 10:16

phrases.english: is the midpoint of the words.
"Vehisgalach" (and he shall be shaved) is the midpoint of the verses.
phrases.notes: ויקרא 13:33

phrases.english: In "The boar from the forest gnaws at it,"
phrases.notes: תהלים 80:14

phrases.english: the ayin of "ya'ar" (forest) is the midpoint of Psalms.
"But He, merciful, forgives sin"
phrases.notes: תהלים 78:38

phrases.english: is its midpoint of verses.
phrases.notes: He means the middle verse of the book of תהלים.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a result ('therefore') from the importance of learning מקרא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The early sages were called סופרים because they counted every letter, word and verse of the תורה and of תהלים.

steps.title: Which half does the vav of גחון belong to?
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף asks whether the middle vav of גחון belongs to the first half of the תורה or the second half.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף asked: The vav of 'gachon', does it belong to this side or to that side?
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף raises a question about the midpoint letter mentioned in the last step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the vav is 'the middle letter', it is not clear whether it ends the first half or begins the second. רב יוסף wants to know exactly where the dividing line falls.

keyTerms.meaning: Belly (the word with the middle letter)

phrases.english: Rav Yosef asked:

phrases.aramaic: וָא״ו ״דְּגָחוֹן״, מֵהַאי גִּיסָא אוֹ מֵהַאי גִּיסָא?
phrases.english: The vav of "gachon": is it from this side or from that side?
phrases.notes: He is asking whether this vav counts with the first half of the תורה or with the second half.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for more detail about the vav of גחון from step 18.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the middle vav of גחון belongs to the first half or the second half of the תורה.

steps.title: Let's just count the letters
steps.stepSummary: The sages suggest bringing a ספר תורה and counting, and point to רבה בר בר חנה, who said that people once did exactly that.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: Let's bring a Torah scroll and count the letters. Didn't רבה בר בר חנה say: They did not move from there until they brought a Torah scroll and counted them?
steps.whatsHappening: The sages offer a simple way to answer רב יוסף's question: count the letters. They support the idea with an earlier case where this was done.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Their point is that counting is a real method that was already used, so the question can be settled by checking. The story of רבה בר בר חנה shows that bringing a ספר תורה to count was an accepted step.

keyTerms.meaning: They did not move from there

phrases.english: They said to him:
Let us bring a Torah scroll and count them.

phrases.aramaic: מִי לָא אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה:
phrases.english: Didn't Rabbah bar bar Chana say:

phrases.aramaic: לֹא זָזוּ מִשָּׁם עַד שֶׁהֵבִיאוּ סֵפֶר תּוֹרָה וּמְנָאוּם?
phrases.english: They did not move from there until they brought a Torah scroll and counted them?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a way to answer רב יוסף's question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The question can be settled by counting the letters in a ספר תורה, as was done in the case reported by רבה בר בר חנה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבה בר בר חנה's report that they brought a ספר תורה and counted the letters.

steps.title: We are not experts in spelling
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף rejects the idea of counting: the earlier sages knew which words are spelled full or short, but we do not, so our count would not be reliable.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: They were experts in missing and extra letters. We are not experts.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף explains why counting the letters will not answer his question today.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Many words in the תורה can be written with or without letters such as vav or yud. The early sages knew the exact spelling of every word, so their counting worked. We no longer know these spellings with certainty, so a count would not settle the question, and it stays open.

keyTerms.meaning: Words spelled 'short' (missing a letter) or 'full' (with an extra letter)

steps.whatToRemember: The early סופרים knew the exact letters of the תורה. Later generations lost some of that exactness in spelling, so רב יוסף's question cannot be settled by counting.

phrases.english: He said to them:
They were experts in missing and extra letters;
phrases.notes: These are words that can be spelled with or without a letter like vav or yud.

phrases.english: we are not experts.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִינְהוּ בְּקִיאִי בַּחֲסֵירוֹת וִיתֵרוֹת, אֲנַן לָא בְּקִיאִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the counting suggestion of step 20.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects counting the letters as a way to answer the question today, not the earlier sages' counting itself.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Today we do not know the exact full and short spellings, so our count would be unreliable.

steps.title: Which half does the verse 'והתגלח' belong to?
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף asks whether the middle verse of the תורה, 'והתגלח', belongs to the first half or the second half.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף asked: The verse 'Then he shall be shaven' – does it belong to this side or to that side?
steps.whatsHappening: Just as he asked about the middle letter, רב יוסף now asks about the middle verse of the תורה. Does 'והתגלח' count with the first half or with the second half?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier the question was about letters (the vav of גחון). Now רב יוסף asks the same kind of question about verses. The verse 'והתגלח' sits right at the dividing point, and he wants to know which side it goes with.

keyTerms.meaning: asked; raised a question he could not answer
'then he shall be shaven' – a verse about a נגע, known as the middle verse of the תורה

phrases.english: Rav Yosef asked:
"Then he shall be shaven"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 13:33. This is the verse known as the middle verse of the תורה.

phrases.english: Is it from this side or from that side?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Parallels רב יוסף's earlier question about the middle letter, now applied to the middle verse.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the middle verse 'והתגלח' belongs to the first half or the second half of the תורה.

steps.title: אביי: At least we can count the verses
steps.stepSummary: אביי suggests that even if we cannot count letters reliably, we can at least bring a ספר תורה and count the verses.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: Verses, at least – let us bring a scroll and count them!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי offers a practical solution: bring a ספר תורה and count the verses to find out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יוסף had already rejected counting letters, because we no longer know which words are spelled full or short. אביי argues that this problem does not apply to verses. Spelling does not change where a verse begins or ends, so counting verses should still work.

phrases.english: Abaye said to him:
Verses, at least, let them bring a scroll and count them!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a way to answer step 22 that gets around רב יוסף's objection in step 21.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Count the verses in a ספר תורה, since spelling questions do not affect how many verses there are.

steps.title: We are not experts in verse divisions either
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף rejects counting verses, because even verse divisions are not certain. In ארץ ישראל they split one verse into three.
steps.simpleTranslation: We are not experts in verses either. When רב אחא בר אדא came, he said: In the West they divide this verse into three verses: 'And ה' said to משה, behold I come to you in a thick cloud.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף answers אביי that counting verses also won't work. He proves it with a report that people in ארץ ישראל divided one verse into three.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If different places divide verses differently, the total number of verses changes, and so does the middle point. The verse in שמות is one verse for us but three verses in ארץ ישראל. So a count would depend on whose divisions you follow, and it cannot settle the question.

phrases.english: In verses, too, we are not experts,

phrases.aramaic: דְּכִי אֲתָא רַב אַחָא בַּר אַדָּא,
phrases.english: for when Rav Aḥa bar Adda came,
he said: In the West they divide
this verse into three verses:
"And the Lord said to Moses,

phrases.aramaic: הִנֵּה אָנֹכִי בָּא אֵלֶיךָ בְּעַב הֶעָנָן״.
phrases.english: behold, I come to you in a thick cloud."
phrases.notes: שמות 19:9.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects אביי's suggestion in step 23.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects counting verses as a way to answer רב יוסף's question.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Verse divisions are not uniform. ארץ ישראל splits a verse into three that we read as one, so any count is unreliable.
steps.whatToRemember: The question of the middle letter and the middle verse stays unanswered. We cannot count letters (spelling is uncertain) or verses (divisions are uncertain).

steps.title: The number of verses in the תורה, תהלים and דברי הימים
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא states that the תורה has 5,888 verses. תהלים has eight more and דברי הימים has eight fewer.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: 5,888 verses are the verses of a ספר תורה. תהלים has eight more than it, and דברי הימים has eight fewer than it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that records the verse counts of the early סופרים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This fits the earlier point that the סופרים counted the verses of the תורה and of תהלים. It gives an exact total for the תורה. It then compares two other books to it: תהלים has 5,896 verses and דברי הימים has 5,880.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
Five thousand eight hundred
and eighty-eight verses
are the verses of a Torah scroll.
Psalms has eight more than it,
Chronicles has eight fewer than it.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: חֲמֵשֶׁת אֲלָפִים וּשְׁמוֹנֶה מֵאוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a related tradition about the counting work of the סופרים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The תורה has 5,888 verses. תהלים has eight more and דברי הימים has eight fewer.

steps.title: 'ושננתם': Torah should be sharp in your mouth
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא learns from 'ושננתם' that a person should know Torah so sharply that he can answer any question right away, without stammering. The proof-verse comes on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: 'And you shall teach them diligently' means that words of Torah should be sharp in your mouth. If a person asks you something, do not stammer and answer him unsure. Rather, answer him immediately, as it says:
steps.whatsHappening: A new topic begins: how well a person must know Torah. The line ends with 'as it is stated', which sets up a פסוק that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'ושננתם' comes from the root שנן, meaning 'sharp'. So the ברייתא reads it as a demand that Torah knowledge be sharp and ready. Being able to say something after hesitating is not enough. You should be able to answer clearly right away.

keyTerms.meaning: 'and you shall teach them diligently' – read here as 'make them sharp'
as it is stated – introduces a פסוק

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught: "And you shall teach them diligently"
phrases.notes: דברים 6:7.

phrases.english: means that words of Torah should be sharp in your mouth,
phrases.notes: The word ושננתם sounds like 'sharpen', which is where this idea comes from.

phrases.english: so that if a person asks you something,
do not stammer and then answer him,
rather, answer him immediately,
as it is stated:

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from counting the תורה to the duty of knowing Torah sharply.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Torah must be known sharply enough to answer any question immediately, without hesitation.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the standard for תלמוד תורה: the goal is ready, clear knowledge, not just having covered the material.
